newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 11.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006 E-mail: biznis@giasdl01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
CONGRESS PARTY CHANGES STAND IN BIHAR STATE

The Bihar state unit of the Congress party said it could support a Rashtriya Janata Dal ministry only if Laloo Prasad Yadav resigned as state chief minister. The Jharkhand Mukti Morcha party also ruled out its support to the Laloo government. The Communist Party of India decided to move the Patna High Court challenging the constitutional validity of a minority government in Bihar. A delegation of senior Congress party leaders called on Congress president Sitaram Kesri and told him supporting Laloo Yadav now would be suicidal. They told Kesri that such a step would lead to largescale desertion by party supporters.
The Economic Times
RUPEE TOUCHES SEVEN MONTH HIGH

The rupee hit a seven-month high against the dollar in the spot market when it closed at 35.7350/7425. The Reserve Bank of India stayed away from the foreign exchange market, in contrast to the RBI's defence of the dollar at the 35.80 rupee level. With the RBI abstaining, the rupee had a field day. Dealers were baffled by the absence of the RBI and the State Bank of India. The RBI was checking the quotes from time to time but did not buy dollars. An obvious reason is the liquidity in the system. Call rates had dipped to 1.5 percent and had the RBI bought dollars, it would only have added to the cash-flush scenario.
INDIA'S MACROECONOMIC OUTLOOK STRONG

The International Monetary Fund has projected a strong macroeconomic outlook for India with emphasis on stable external sector growth. The IMF said strong capital inflows into the country would continue this year and raise the value of rupee against the dollar. To mitigate the larger effects of accelerated capital inflows, the government must reduce its fiscal deficit and simultaneously liberalise the trade regime by lifting quantative restrictions on imports, the IMF internal report on India's current status said.
COUNTERVAILING DUTY ON SUGAR PLANNED

The Finance Ministry is considering a proposal to immediately impose countervailing duty (CVD) on sugar. A Food Ministry note said either the CVD or a levy on sugar should be immediately imposed to ward off the dumping of foreign sugar in India. The ministry suggested a CVD of 20 percent to 30 percent to effectively deter private traders. If the Finance Ministry refuses to introduce CVD on sugar, the Food Ministry will impose a levy on imported sugar under the existing laws.
Financial Express
NEW PRIVATE BANKS GROW BY 10 PERCENT

Fuelled by high export credit, the new generation of private banks recorded a 10 percent growth in credit offtake between April and June 1997, against a 0.6 percent negative credit growth in the entire banking industry. During the fortnight ended June 20, bank credit in all scheduled commercial banks showed a negative growth of 15.86 billion rupees. The only new private bank that recorded negative growth was the Times Bank, which saw its advances dropping by nearly 11 percent over its March figure. The Unit Trust of India Bank recorded the highest growth with a 41 percent growth in its advances.
POWER PURCHASE AGREEMENTS MAY BE REVISED

The power purchase agreements (PPAs) signed by independent power producers with state governments are likely to be renegotiated following the announcement of the federal government's liquid fuel policy. If all of the naphtha needed to generate the projected 12,000 megawatts is to be imported, its prices in the international markets may increase considerably. The independent power producers will have to bear the cost of creating facilities for importing naphtha and other liquid fuels and for carrying these to the project sites. For these two reasons, the Power Ministry feels that the cost of naphtha-based power plants will go up.
Business Standard
UMBRELLA INSURANCE COVER FOR INDUSTRY OFFERED

The General Insurance Corporation has launched an industrial all-risk insurance policy with effect from July 1. It is meant for customers who have insured an overall amount of one billion rupees or more in one or more locations in the country. The policy offers an umbrella cover for material damages and business interruption losses, including loss of profit. It will allow companies to buy covers for a variety of risks at lower rates and opt for deductibles.
STIFF NORMS FOR ENTRY INTO POWER TRANSMISSION

A committee on power transmission has recommended that a company which owns a power station in a region should not be allowed to set up any transmission projects in the same region. It also recommended that state electricity boards should lay down strict eligibility criteria for developers of transmission projects. The eligibility criteria will vary depending on the state and the region in which the transmission project will come up. The report by the Shankar Guruswamy committee leaves it to the states to decide whether to opt for a one-stage or two-stage competitive bidding process to select developers of transmission projects.
The Observer
INDIA MAY MISS IMF DEADLINE

India may not be able to honour the December 1998 deadline set by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for becoming a full-fledged subscriber to the Standardised Data Destination System (SDDS). As per the norms of the SDDS, member countries of the IMF should furnish macro-statistics on 17 important segments of economic activity falling under the real, external and financial sectors. Sources said many departments were yet to decide on how to start with the data collection since many of the existing methods were inefficient to meet the IMF criteria. The third inter-ministerial meeting held to review the progress of the data collection feared India might not be able to meet the IMF deadline.
